newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols decline after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols decline after FOMC.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options pulled back Tuesday in the wake of the Federal Open Market Committee's monetary policy meeting.

U.S. central bankers left short-term interest rates unchanged amid continued evidence of moderate economic growth and low inflation. The key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans stands at 5.5 percent.
October bond volatility slipped to 8.25 percent at the session's end from 8.40 percent on the opening and 8.65 percent the previous session.
Volatility for September options, which expire at the end of the week, fell to 7.0 percent from 7.8 percent at the opening, while December edged down to 8.6 percent from 8.7 percent.

Bond options activity was hushed as the market focused on the outcome of the Fed meeting, traders said. Expectations that bond prices are likely to be confined to a range near term also stifled interest in trading options, they said.
At the short end, Eurodollar volatilities eased substantially after heavy buying of December 94.25 calls and stock market jitters had pumped up values during the previous two sessions, brokers said.
December fell back to 7.5 percent from 9.0 percent previously and March dropped to 10.8 percent from 11.5 percent.
"I don't think vols are going to get much lower," said one Eurodollar options trader. "The market's shown that it can move every now and then."

A U.S. bank that had been a huge buyer of the 94.25 December calls outright and in spreads against sales of 94.25 puts in recent days turned around and sold 5,000 of the calls today, floor traders said.
Other firms were noted buying 93.75/94.00 put spreads and selling 94.00 straddles in December, and one bank bought 1,200 June 94.00 straddles.
